name: Anton Dove
life: Anton knows which ward windows fog first and which patients would rather see streetlights than the sea. His eldest boy thinks he pushes beds for a living. Both descriptions are accurate, which pleases him. Wednesday often includes a stop at the corner outside Coastal Barber, where Anton usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: Window seven is the first place I saw the sea after I moved here. I timed the empty corridor with my watch and asked the patient what counted as sunrise to her.
appearance: Anton has auburn hair cut square at the nape, a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling, and a favorite piece of clothing, a moss-green cardigan. It usually goes with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case. When somebody else has the floor, Anton listens with the head tilted a little to the left.
personality: Anton takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Anton can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To work out a clear route to window seven before sunrise.
family: Bruna Morse is Anton’s half-sibling. Anton asks before bringing somebody along. Bruna can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *Nine unpaid hours*, Bruna says, “I ran payroll. I warned management on Wednesday and told the crews on Friday.”
connections: Lois Fell (ward colleague). The porter knows this window. The chaplain is discovering how much of the morning that knowledge can hold.

reactions.response: Anton asks the patient whether they want a camera in this particular morning.
